THE RUN-28 BRIEF'S EXPECTATION IS HALF REFUTED. The reloc-naming classifier was requested precisely so that 'several genuine counts will drop' on the leads it queued - and it did NOT drop them. fn_80062A00 (21) and fn_8005BA1C (22) carry ZERO reloc-naming rows and their genuine counts are bit-identical to run 27. Where the classifier paid was elsewhere: it retired fn_8005D730 from 5 genuine to 1, and it surfaced FOUR functions that no prior census listed at all (fn_8005D3D8, fn_8005D5C8, fn_8005DE50, fn_8005EE18), every one of them 100% artifact and correctly requiring no work. GENERAL LESSON: a new classifier's value is not concentrated on the rows the previous census ranked highest - re-run it over the WHOLE roster, not over the queued leads.

THE RUN-27 FRAME LEADS, RE-MEASURED. Lead (a), 'fn_8005F0F4 is 8 BYTES OVER, find the surplus declared local', IS REFUTED AS STATED and was worth far more than it claimed. slotdiff reports frame target 296 / ours 296 with the same r25 save-set; the census had read `stmw r25,220(r1)` vs `stmw r25,228(r1)` as a frame delta when it is a SAVE-AREA delta - the target saves SIX callee-saved FPRs (_savefpr_26) and we saved five. The 8 bytes are real but they are the price of the missing sixth FPR, and the sixth FPR is a missing SOURCE VARIABLE, not a pad: our reconstruction had overwritten the base collision radius with a+R and then subtracted the wrong one. See attempt.GW_fn8005f0f4-missing-radius-variable-and-frame-reseat.20260901.v1. METHOD NOTE for future frame leads: read the save-set and the FPR web counts BEFORE reading the stmw displacement - `stmw` offset alone cannot distinguish a frame change from a save-area change.
